title: Yara and the Postcard
premise: Yara Lindqvist, granddaughter of a lighthouse keeper and author of modestly successful novels, has built her life on staying small in the coastal town of Haven's End. When a postcard she wrote eleven years ago—and never sent—to Gideon Eriksen, the man she loved and abandoned for a publishing career, surfaces in her late grandmother's attic, it forces her to confront the night she chose ambition over truth. Gideon, now the town's beloved harbormaster and engaged to the mayor's daughter, receives the postcard just as Yara's publisher pressures her to write a tell-all memoir that would expose his family's role in a decades-old land deal. As the autumn lantern festival approaches, Yara must decide whether to publish the memoir that will save her career but destroy Gideon's standing, or burn the manuscript and risk losing everything she built. She chooses truth over safety—but rewrites the ending, confessing her own complicity first, and in the final chapter, at the festival's lantern release, Gideon chooses her, ending his engagement and asking for a second chance with better timing.
about_author: Edmund Fairweather is the pen name of a former small-town newspaper editor who spent fifteen years covering harbor towns before turning to fiction. He writes quiet romances about people who almost missed their lives.

chapters.title: The Attic Smell of Old Paper
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Clearing her late grandmother's attic, Yara finds a box of unsent letters, including a postcard in her own handwriting to Gideon, postmarked but never delivered. The emotional beat is dread disguised as nostalgia; she pockets the postcard before her sister can see it.

chapters.title: Eleven Years of Careful Smallness
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Flashback-tinged present-day chapter establishing Yara's routine: teaching writing workshops, her modest novel sales, her deliberate invisibility in Haven's End. Beat: the comfortable armor of a life built to avoid risk.

chapters.title: The Harbormaster's Morning
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Gideon inspects the harbor, plans his engagement announcement for the lantern festival, and is quietly, stubbornly content—until he notices Yara's name on a workshop flyer. Beat: a hairline crack in a settled life.

chapters.title: What the Postcard Said
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Alone at the lighthouse, Yara rereads her eleven-year-old postcard: an apology and a confession she never had the courage to send. Beat: shame resurfacing, and the first pull toward honesty.

chapters.title: The Publisher's Ultimatum
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, with a phone call structure. Her publisher, Marisol, proposes a memoir: 'The Lighthouse Keeper's Granddaughter,' promising an advance that would pay off Yara's debts—if she includes the Eriksen family's buried land deal. Beat: temptation wearing the mask of opportunity.

chapters.title: Tea with the Mayor's Daughter
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. His fiancée Celeste organizes the festival, charming and ambitious, and mentions the famous novelist returning to town. Beat: Gideon's unease he can't name, loyalty presented as a cage with velvet bars.

chapters.title: Collision at the Fish Market
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Yara and Gideon meet for the first time in eleven years among the stalls; the conversation is polite, brittle, and charged. Beat: the past refusing to stay past.

chapters.title: The Land Deal
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Researching the memoir, Yara uncovers how Gideon's father and the town council cheated her grandfather out of the lighthouse parcel decades ago—and that her grandmother knew, and stayed silent. Beat: betrayal compounding betrayal; the ground shifting under her.

chapters.title: A Drink Neither Planned
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Gideon seeks Yara out to ask what she's writing; one drink becomes three hours of honesty about grief, ambition, and the night she left. Beat: intimacy rekindling against both their wills.

chapters.title: Celeste Reads the Draft
chapters.summary: Celeste's POV. Discovering Yara's manuscript pages at Gideon's office, Celeste reads the land-deal chapter and recognizes the threat to her family's name and her engagement. Beat: Celeste shifts from rival to strategist; power begins to corrupt gently.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Celeste's POV. Celeste offers Yara a deal: bury the land-deal chapter and Celeste will fund her own imprint—or refuse, and Celeste will ruin Yara's credibility town-wide before the festival. Beat: Yara cornered; duty to her grandmother's memory versus survival.

chapters.title: What Grandmother Knew
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. In her grandmother's journals, Yara learns the old woman stayed silent to protect Gideon's family from ruin—and to protect Yara from a town that punishes truth-tellers. Beat: grief and fury braided together; the theme of loyalty vs. truth crystallized.

chapters.title: The Almost-Kiss
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the lighthouse during a storm, Gideon and Yara nearly cross the line; he pulls back, honor-bound, and asks her directly what the memoir will cost him. Beat: Yara lies by omission; the crack becomes a fault line.

chapters.title: Marisol's Deadline
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Marisol gives Yara 48 hours: deliver the full manuscript before the festival or lose the contract and the advance. Beat: the clock starts; career pressure at maximum.

chapters.title: Celeste's Counterstrike
chapters.summary: Celeste's POV. Celeste leaks a rumor that Yara's memoir is a revenge fantasy, turning the town's goodwill cold; shopkeepers Yara has known for years go quiet. Beat: isolation; the cost of being visible at last.

chapters.title: The Postcard Delivered
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Gideon finally learns of the postcard—Celeste, weaponizing it, shows him the eleven-year-old confession to prove Yara's pattern of abandonment. Beat: heartbreak weaponized; Gideon's trust shatters.

chapters.title: Burning the Manuscript
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. On the eve of the festival, Yara burns the memoir draft in her grandfather's old stove—then realizes she's repeating her grandmother's silence. Beat: the false resolution; she nearly chooses safety and self-erasure.

chapters.title: The Festival Begins
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Lantern festival: Celeste's engagement announcement looms, Marisol calls with a final offer, and Yara watches Gideon across the crowd. Beat: every thread pulled taut; the town as witness.

chapters.title: The Truth, Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. At the festival's open-mic, Yara reads not from her novel but from her grandmother's journals and her own confession—including her eleven years of silence and the unsent postcard. Beat: climax; truth offered at the price of everything.

chapters.title: What Gideon Chooses
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Stunned, Gideon ends the engagement publicly but gently, confronts his father's legacy, and walks through the crowd toward Yara. Beat: the second turning point—love chosen over duty and reputation.

chapters.title: Rewriting the Ending
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Days later, Yara signs a revised memoir deal—one that leads with her own complicity—and mails a new letter, this time with a return address. Beat: quiet resolution; visibility chosen and survived.

chapters.title: The Lighthouse at Dawn
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Gideon arrives at the relit lighthouse at dawn; Yara shows him the postcard's answer she wrote at seventeen and the one she wrote last night. They begin again, without guarantees. Beat: hopeful, earned resolution—second chances, finally, for people with better timing.
